title: Apply a strict unified diff subset
instructions:
Implement a parser and applier for a deliberately limited, single-file unified diff.
All inputs are strings containing only LF line separators (no CR). Do not read files.

## Files
- `diff_parser.py`
- `patcher.py`

In `diff_parser.py`, provide a dataclass `Hunk` with fields `old_start: int`,
`old_count: int`, `new_start: int`, `new_count: int`, and
`lines: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]` (prefix, content).
`parse_patch(patch) -> list[Hunk]` follows these rules:
- The empty string means no hunks. Otherwise the first two lines must start with
  `--- ` and `+++ ` respectively and have nonempty labels after those prefixes.
  Labels are ignored. Header-only patches are allowed.
- Hunk headers exactly match `@@ -N[,C] +N[,C] @@` with ASCII nonnegative decimal
  integers; omitted counts mean 1. For a positive count its start must be >= 1.
  Count zero allows start zero. Leading zeros in header numbers are allowed.
- Each body line begins with one of space, `-`, `+`. Store the rest verbatim,
  including empty content and trailing spaces. Space consumes an old and a new
  line, minus only an old line, plus only a new line. Counts must exactly match
  the body through the next hunk header or EOF. Blank unprefixed lines and all
  other syntax (including no-newline markers and section labels) are invalid.
- The patch may have or omit one final LF; it is a line terminator, not a body line.
  Any malformed patch raises `ValueError`. Ordering/position checks belong to the applier.

`patcher.apply_patch(original, patch) -> str` uses `parse_patch` and applies hunks:
- Original text must be empty or end in LF; otherwise raise `ValueError`, even for
  an empty patch. Split it into content lines, preserving blank lines/spaces.
- For a nonzero old_count, the original zero-based index is old_start-1. For zero
  old_count, it is old_start (insertion after that many original lines).
  Hunk positions always refer to the original, not the partially changed text.
- Hunks must be ordered and nonoverlapping: each index must be >= the original
  cursor after the previous hunk, and <= the original line count. Equal indices
  are allowed for consecutive zero-old-count insertions, in patch order.
- Copy unchanged gaps first. At each hunk, the new-file zero-based index
  (new_start-1 if new_count>0, otherwise new_start) must equal the number of output
  lines already produced. Reject inconsistent new coordinates with `ValueError`.
- Space and minus lines must exactly match the next original line, otherwise
  `ValueError`; reject consumption past EOF. Emit space and plus contents; omit
  minus contents. Copy the untouched suffix after all hunks.
- Return LF-terminated output if there are any lines, otherwise `''`. An empty
  or header-only patch returns the original unchanged. Propagate parser errors.
